newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish opposition seeks no-confidence vote in PM.
newsitem.headline: Swedish opposition seeks no-confidence vote in PM.

text.p: Three Swedish opposition parties said on Wednesday they would seek a no-confidence vote in Parliament over Prime Minister Goran Persson's comments during a visit to China, when he appeared to praise Beijing.
The opposition Conservative, Liberal and Christian Democratic parties filed their bid for the vote after a special parliamentary debate.

Persson angered Swedish politicians during an official visit to Beijing this month when he made what were seen to be complimentary remarks about China's political stability. The ensuing row over his comments prompted a special meeting of the foreign policy advisory committee, chaired by the king, and Wednesday's debate in parliament.

Political analysts, however, said it was unlikely a vote of no confidence would suceed against Persson, leader of the ruling Social Democratic Party, who took to the helm in March this year, replacing the retiring Ingvar Carlsson.
Persson runs a minority government which survives with the support of a leftist party, but he has been moving towards forming a coalition with the Centre Party.
